in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek 'Alphos' meaning 'man' and 'phon' meaning 'El', the Greek god of the heavens. The name Alphonso is not directly attested in the New Testament, but it is a common given name in the Greek-speaking world.

in_latin.name: Alphonso
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin 'Alphonsus', derived from the Latin words 'albus' meaning 'white' or 'noble' and 'ponsus' meaning 'bearer' or 'supporter'. This name was borne by several saints in the Middle Ages.

in_english.name: Alphonso
in_english.long_meaning: From the Old English 'alf' meaning 'elf' or 'all' and 'fons' meaning 'source' or 'spring'. In the Middle Ages, the name Alphonso was sometimes used as a variant of the Old English name 'Alfred', meaning 'elf-counsel' or 'wise elf'. However, the modern English form of the name is more likely derived from the Latin 'Alphonsus', as explained above.

It was borne by several kings and saints, including Alfonso X of Castile and Alfonso I of Aragon. The name's regal associations continued into the Renaissance era, where it was adopted by wealthy and influential families in Europe.
